prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-facing outdoor scene where the camera wearer squats or leans over a brick walkway on the left and a raised garden bed bordered by a low metal fence on the right, with two bags of mulch on the ground about 0.5–1.0 m below and in front of the viewpoint. The wearer's own hands, forearms, and knees are the brightest and nearest elements at roughly 0.2–0.6 m (well within arm's reach, along with the open mulch bag, the adjacent closed bag 0.2 m to its left, the fence, and overhanging hydrangea foliage at 0.4–0.8 m), while in frames 2 and 5 the ground plane recedes into dark values toward a parked white car's wheel (about 2–3 m to the left) and a second person's lower legs standing 3–4 m ahead at the top edge. Across the five frames, the viewpoint pans left and tilts up in frame 2, turns back right and pitches down closer to the open bag in frames 3–4 as the right arm rises to 0.2–0.3 m in front of the camera while occluding the bag interior, and pans slightly left again in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the 3D layering of the overhanging leaves, the raised rim of the open plastic bag, and the elevated right forearm against the dark soil background. However, it is unreliable inside the open bag where dark mulch is rendered as a flat recess, and at the top of frames 2 and 5 where the distant standing person's feet and the car wheel blend into the dark background gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates parts of the camera wearer in the lower foreground (0.2–0.6 m away) and a second person at the top edge of frame 2 (roughly 3–4 m ahead and 2–3 m beyond the mulch bags), while leaving the brick pavement, garden bed, and bags unmasked in black. In frame 2, the distant person is visible only by their feet and lower legs at the upper-left edge—facing roughly toward the walkway with their upper body cropped out of view and unable to be seen looking toward the wearer—while a white car wheel sits at the far left edge about 2–3 m away. Across frames 1 to 4, the wearer's visible limbs shift from a single right arm reaching toward the garden bed on the right (frame 1), to two separate masks for the left and right forearms/legs flanking the open bag (frame 2), to a single merged mask covering the right arm, knees, and torso in the lower-right and center as the wearer reaches into and lifts mulch from the bag within arm's reach (frames 3–4), before all masks disappear in frame 5. The map highlights the distant person's feet at the top of frame 2 that are easy to miss in the wide-angle RGB strip, and tracks how the wearer's limbs self-occlude the lower foreground. However, it is highly unreliable across the sequence: it misclassifies a small green plant in the soil bed as 'broccoli' (frame 1) and the car wheel on the left as a 'clock' (frame 2), merges the wearer's limbs and the held mulch into a single 'person' region in frame 4, and completely fails to detect any people or objects in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map renders magenta hand keypoints for the camera wearer's hands in the foreground (0.2–0.6 m from the camera, within immediate arm's reach of the mulch bags and plants) across all five frames, along with a yellow body skeleton in frame 4, while the distant person 3–4 m away in frames 2 and 5 is completely omitted because their torso and head are out of view. Across the sequence, the tracked magenta hand skeleton shifts from the right hand reaching into the right-hand garden bed in frame 1, to the left hand gripping the open plastic bag's rim in the lower center-left in frames 2 and 3 (about 0.5 m below the camera), to both hands converging near the bag opening in frame 4 (spaced about 0.15 m apart as the right hand holds a clump of mulch above the left hand), and back to the left hand at the lower-left of the bag in frame 5. In frame 4, the map reveals the fine finger articulation of both the left hand holding the bag and the dirt-covered right hand grasping dark mulch, which blends into the dark soil in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable where it misses the right hand while it is partially occluded inside the bag in frames 2 and 3, and in frame 4 where it hallucinates a compact yellow full-body and facial keypoint cluster directly on top of the wearer's crouched right forearm and knee as if a miniature person were facing the camera.
